To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AMPK β1 knockout mice have less renal fibrosis in early diabetes, despite higher blood glucose levels.
AMPK activation worsens renal fibrosis in diabetes, despite increased circulating levels of glucose.
the absence of AMPK β‐subunit in AMPK β1 knockout mice reduces the number of myofibrocytes in the kidneys of type 1 diabetic mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of the AMP‐activated protein Kinase (AMPK) in diabetic kidney disease (DKD).
understanding the role of the AMPK β‐subunit in the pathogenesis of diabetes.
the effect of AMPK on diabetic kidney disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AMPK β1‐null mice have a reduced myofibrocyte population in their diabetic kidneys, despite increased plasma glucose, and that this may contribute to reduced albuminuria.
AMPK activation does not improve, and can even worsen, diabetic nephropathy.
AMPK activation is not beneficial in diabetic kidney disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AMPK activation in diabetes is associated with increased renal myofibrobalsts and albuminuria.
the absence of the β1‐subunit of AMPK reduces the severity of diabetic kidney disease in mice, and that this may be mediated via a reduction of renal myofibroplasia.
AMPK activation is not beneficial in type 1 diabetic kidneys and may even be detrimental, and this may be due to the increased phosphorylation of the AMPK α‐subunit inhibitory site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AMPK β1‐null mice are more susceptible to hyperglycaemia, but have fewer myofiboblasts in the kidney compared to WT mice.
AMPK activation is not a universal solution for the treatment of diabetic kidney disease.
the β1 subunits of AMPK are important regulators of renal fibrosis and albuminuria in early diabetes.
